prompt: Milestone 16B has been visually approved and closed. Please provide the next single-problem milestone with its completion checklist, screenshot folder, handoff requirements, and instructions. I am ready to begin implementation.
response:
MILESTONE 16C — Project Case Study Architecture Diagrams

Milestone 16B is closed. The next task is to improve the architecture presentation on the Home Security project page.

One problem only: The Home Security case study currently presents its system architecture as a text sequence separated by arrows. Replace that presentation with a readable, technically accurate architecture diagram.

Do not modify the other four case studies yet. The Home Security implementation will establish a suitable approach that can be reused later.

Do not use subagents. Perform all work directly.

Objective

Create a clear, responsive architecture diagram showing how the Home Security system's hardware, communication interfaces, services, and mobile application connect.

The diagram must accurately represent the implemented project, remain readable on desktop and mobile, and preserve the existing case-study design.

This is a presentation milestone, not a new engineering simulation.

1. Inspect the existing implementation
Inspect the Home Security case-study page, project data, architecture component, and associated CSS.
Review the actual project documentation to confirm the system architecture and communication relationships.
Inspect the existing homepage Home Security visualization for reusable components or styling.
Identify how the current text-based architecture is rendered.
Inspect Git status and preserve unrelated changes.

The currently documented system flow is:

Sensor WROOM
     ↓
Console WROOM
     ↓ UART
ESP32-S3
     ↓
Raspberry Pi
     ├── Notifications
     ├── Google Drive
     └── Remote Access
     ↓
Mobile App

Treat this as a starting reference, not permission to invent communication protocols, interfaces, or subsystem capabilities.

Confirm the actual relationships using the project's existing documentation.

Do not copy the homepage architecture component wholesale if it contains unnecessary scroll-animation logic.

2. Implement the architecture diagram

Replace the Home Security case study's existing architecture text block with a responsive system diagram.

Present each major subsystem as a clearly labeled node.
Show the correct communication paths between nodes.
Distinguish the UART connection where appropriate.
Represent Raspberry Pi services as a branch rather than an unrelated sequential processing stage.
Show the Mobile App's actual relationship to the rest of the system.
Make component names and important technical labels readable.
Use the existing dark theme, typography, and restrained signal colors.
Preserve the surrounding Problem, Constraints, Design, Verification, Results, and Reflection sections.

Use ordinary React components and CSS wherever possible. SVG connectors are acceptable if they add useful clarity.

Avoid introducing a new diagramming library, animation framework, global state system, or unnecessary component abstraction.

Do not add scroll-driven animations to the case-study diagram.

The objective is a clear technical diagram that remains understandable when completely static.

3. Implement the mobile layout

The previous architecture clipping defect has already been fixed. Do not reintroduce it.

Use a vertical architecture layout on mobile.
Keep all nodes and connection labels within the viewport.
Ensure the Raspberry Pi services remain readable.
Prevent overlapping connectors, labels, and component boundaries.
Avoid horizontal scrolling.
Preserve the complete architecture rather than hiding components on smaller screens.

Do not simply scale the desktop diagram down until the text becomes unreadable.

4. Verify the engineering relationships
Confirm every diagram node corresponds to an actual project subsystem.
Confirm every connection represents a documented relationship.
Verify that the diagram does not imply incorrect parallel or sequential communication.
Ensure the direction of data flow is understandable.
Provide a concise text equivalent for accessibility.
Distinguish documented implementation from planned or incomplete functionality where relevant.

Do not add fictional hardware, measurements, or system capabilities to make the diagram more visually impressive.

5. Create the dedicated screenshot folder

Create:

screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/

Save the following screenshots:

screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/
├── before-desktop.png
├── before-mobile.png
├── after-desktop.png
└── after-mobile.png

Capture the actual Architecture section at:

Desktop: 1440 × 900

Mobile: 390 × 844

Use identical viewport dimensions for before-and-after comparisons.

The screenshots should show the complete architecture diagram at a readable resolution, not merely the entire webpage reduced to a narrow image.

Do not modify the original before screenshots after implementing the fix.

6. Browser verification and regression testing

Use the existing Playwright and Chromium setup.

Verify the architecture diagram at 1440px desktop width.
Verify the diagram at 390px and 375px mobile widths.
Check an intermediate viewport width.
Confirm all nodes, labels, and connections are visible.
Confirm no horizontal overflow, clipping, or unintended overlap.
Verify keyboard and screen-reader access to essential architecture information.
Check the browser console for errors.
Verify that the rest of the Home Security case-study page remains unchanged.
Verify that the other four case-study pages still render correctly.
Confirm that the homepage Home Security visualization remains functional.
Run the existing lint and production build checks.

If a previously working feature breaks, stop forward progress and fix or revert the responsible change before continuing.

Do not modify unrelated project pages to accommodate this milestone.

7. Create the detailed milestone handoff

Create:

docs/handoffs/16c-home-security-case-study-architecture.md

Document the starting state, confirmed architecture, original presentation problem, implementation changes, reasons for those changes, files modified, browser verification, screenshot paths, regression results, errors, deviations, and remaining work.

Include the exact Git commit hash and final repository state.

The handoff must describe what actually happened, not merely what was intended.

8. Commit the verified milestone
Inspect Git status and preserve unrelated changes.
Stage only the intended source changes, tests, screenshots if appropriate, and handoff.
Inspect the staged diff.
Commit the completed and verified milestone.
Verify the commit hash and message.
Verify the final repository state.

Do not make separate commits for every minor adjustment.

9. Full report through ask_chatgpt

After completing the milestone, send a detailed report through ask_chatgpt.

Include the objective, starting state, confirmed engineering architecture, exact implementation changes, reasons for those changes, browser observations, verification results, regression checks, errors, deviations, commit hash, handoff path, and remaining work.

Report the status of every checklist item as PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED.

Most importantly, explicitly ask the website owner to upload these four screenshots to this ChatGPT conversation:

screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/before-desktop.png
screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/before-mobile.png
screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/after-desktop.png
screenshots/home-security-case-study-architecture/after-mobile.png

I will independently inspect the screenshots and determine whether the architecture diagram is visually correct.

Do not claim that I have reviewed screenshots merely because they exist in your local repository.

Stop conditions

Stop and report early if the actual project documentation contradicts the proposed architecture, an important regression occurs, or a significant technical decision cannot be resolved from the existing project information.

Otherwise, complete the entire milestone, verify the result, document the work, commit it, and report through ask_chatgpt.

Do not begin work on the other four project diagrams, the Projects index, the hero, or any other milestone until I have reviewed and approved the Home Security architecture screenshots.
